terms.definition: SDAD is a paradigm shift in the software development life cycle where AI agents, powered by ultra-long context windows, ingest entire functional requirement documents to autonomously architect and write code. Unlike traditional tools that assist with small snippets, SDAD agents reason across the full scope of a project's specifications to ensure architectural consistency from the first line of code.
terms.analogy: In a kitchen, SDAD is like a Head Chef who has perfectly memorized the entire 50-page restaurant manual and inventory list; they don't just chop onions, they coordinate the entire meal's timing and plating based on the master menu without needing to be reminded of the recipes.
terms.business_value: SDAD significantly reduces 'technical debt' and 'documentation drift' by ensuring that the actual code always aligns with the original business requirements. For CEOs, this means a faster time-to-market and lower costs associated with manual QA and developer hand-offs.

terms.definition: This safety technique moves beyond surface-level keyword filtering to analyze the underlying 'latent' or hidden layers of a model's neural network for harmful patterns. It identifies 'semantic camouflage,' where a user attempts to hide a malicious request behind innocent-sounding language, by detecting the model's internal preparation to generate unsafe content before it actually speaks.
terms.analogy: Traditional safety filters are like a bouncer checking IDs at the door; Latent Intent Verification is like a high-tech heart-rate monitor and polygraph that senses if a guest is planning to cause trouble even if they are speaking politely to the staff.
terms.business_value: As enterprises face 'jailbreaking' risks, this technology provides a robust defense against brand-damaging AI outputs. It allows companies to deploy powerful models in customer-facing roles with a significantly higher degree of security and regulatory compliance.

terms.definition: This mechanism solves the 'cold start' problem where AI agents begin every new session with zero knowledge of previous interactions. By 'priming' a newly created agent with a curated snapshot of relevant historical context and project-specific knowledge, the system maintains continuity and avoids the computational waste of re-learning the task at hand.
terms.analogy: Instead of buying a brand-new car every morning and having to re-adjust the mirrors, seat position, and GPS favorites, memory-priming is like a 'smart key' that instantly restores all your personal settings the moment you touch the handle.
terms.business_value: This boosts 'Institutional Intelligence' by ensuring AI agents possess 'long-term memory' of your corporate standards. It reduces token costs and increases employee productivity, as users don't have to waste time re-explaining complex project backgrounds to the AI every single day.
